question: If the correlation coefficient between two variables is zero, then the two lines of regression will be:
solution:
The correct answer is** perpendicular to each other.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Two lines of regression will be perpendicular to each other if the correlation coefficient between two variables is zero:**

 
 
• In the context of financial enterprises, the regression lines represent the relationship between two financial variables, such as stock prices and trading volume.
 
• When the correlation coefficient is zero, it indicates that there is no linear relationship between the two variables.
 
• In such a scenario, the slopes of the regression lines are negative reciprocals of each other, making the lines perpendicular.
 
• This perpendicularity reflects the lack of any predictable pattern between the variables, which can be crucial in financial risk assessment and decision-making.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallel to each other:**

 
 
• This is incorrect. If the regression lines were parallel, it would imply a constant difference between the variables, which does not align with a zero correlation coefficient.
 
 
 
• **Coincide with each other:**
 
 
• This is incorrect. Coinciding regression lines would suggest a perfect linear relationship, either positive or negative, corresponding to a correlation coefficient of +1 or -1, not zero.
 
 
 
• **Overlap with each other:**
 
 
• This is incorrect. Overlapping regression lines would again indicate a perfect correlation, not zero.
